sections.markdown:
## C — Signs and signals part one: sign color codes, regulatory signs, lane-use and limited-use lanes, disability parking, warning signs including railroad, school, pedestrian, slow-moving vehicle and intersection signs, construction signs, service and guide signs, dark signals and intersection gridlock
Knowledge domain: what Minnesota road signs mean by color and wording, what each regulatory, warning and construction sign requires the driver to do, and what to do when a traffic signal is out or an intersection is backed up. The manual pairs each sign with a picture; only the printed text meanings are used here.

FACT_ID: sec09-F01 | anchor: A01
Minnesota's signs, signals and pavement markings follow national standards. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-F02 | anchor: A01
Sign shapes and colors are coded so that you can grasp a sign's general meaning before you are close enough to read it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-F03 | anchor: A01
On regulatory signs, red prohibits and commands, while white regulates. [A01]
Why it matters: red versus white is a common color-code item.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-F04 | anchor: A01
On warning signs, yellow warns, yellow-green warns and controls at pedestrian and bicycle crossings and school areas, and orange warns and controls in construction zones. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-F05 | anchor: A01
On informational signs, green guides and informs, blue describes motorist services, and brown marks historic, cultural or recreational sites. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-F06 | anchor: A02
Regulatory signs require you to follow traffic laws, and ignoring one can bring a traffic citation and a fine. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F07 | anchor: A02
At a Stop sign, come to a full stop and wait until every pedestrian and vehicle that has the right-of-way is out of the intersection, then go on with caution. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F08 | anchor: A02
At a Yield sign, slow down or stop if necessary and give the right-of-way to all other vehicles and pedestrians until it is safe to go. [A02]
Why it matters: stop versus yield is a classic sign item.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F09 | anchor: A02
A Do Not Enter sign facing you means you may not enter that lane or road. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F10 | anchor: A02
A Wrong Way sign means you have entered a lane of oncoming traffic and are traveling in the wrong direction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F11 | anchor: A02
A red circle with a red slash across a symbol, as on No Left Turn, No Right Turn, No U Turn and No Parking signs, means the action shown is not allowed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F12 | anchor: A02
A speed limit sign shows the maximum speed for the road, and controlled-access interstate freeways may also post minimum limits that you must not go below unless bad weather or poor road conditions require it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F13 | anchor: A02
The regulatory Do Not Pass sign marks where a no-passing zone begins. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F14 | anchor: A03
A One Way sign means traffic in that lane moves only in the direction of the arrow. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec09-F15 | anchor: A03
A Keep Right sign tells you to stay to the right of a traffic island, median or obstruction ahead. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec09-F16 | anchor: A03
Before a multilane roundabout, signs show which lane to use for each turn, so move into the correct lane well in advance, for example the right lane only to turn right and the left lane only to turn left. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec09-F17 | anchor: A03
A lane-use control sign means you must turn if you are in the lane it marks, though a sign may also show that one lane can go straight or turn. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec09-F18 | anchor: A03
A No Turn on Red sign means you wait for a green signal before turning. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec09-F19 | anchor: A03
A center lane left-turn only sign means traffic from both directions shares the center lane and may use it only to make left turns. [A03]
Why it matters: the shared center turn lane is a likely test item.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec09-F20 | anchor: A04
A Reduced Speed Ahead sign means a lower speed limit is coming, so begin slowing down. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec09-F21 | anchor: A04
A diamond symbol marks a lane reserved for certain uses or vehicles, such as cars with two or more passengers, buses, commercial vehicles or bicycles. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec09-F22 | anchor: A04
Only vehicles carrying disability license plates or a disability parking permit may use spaces marked with blue disability parking signs. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec09-F23 | anchor: A04
If the designated disability spaces are full or unavailable, a driver with a valid disability permit or plates may park at an angle across two standard spaces. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec09-F24 | anchor: A04
Most warning signs are yellow, but pedestrian crossing, bicycle crossing and school zone signs may be yellow or fluorescent yellow-green. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec09-F25 | anchor: A04
Pavement markings in front of a railroad crossing include a stop line, an X and the letters RR. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec09-F26 | anchor: A04
An X-shaped crossbuck sign marks a railroad crossing, and when there is more than one track, a sign below it shows how many. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec09-F27 | anchor: A04
An exempt sign at a railroad crossing lets bus and truck drivers who normally must stop go on without stopping, though they must still look both ways for trains. [A04]
Why it matters: the exempt sign is a frequently missed item.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec09-F28 | anchor: A05
Railroad crossing ahead signs mean slow down, look carefully both ways and be ready to stop, because trains cannot stop quickly. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-F29 | anchor: A05
Pentagon-shaped school zone signs, yellow or fluorescent yellow-green, warn that a school or an approved school crosswalk is ahead, so watch for children and be ready to stop. [A05]
Why it matters: the pentagon shape belongs to school signs.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-F30 | anchor: A05
At a school crossing sign, watch for children and be ready to stop, since drivers must yield to every pedestrian in a crosswalk. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-F31 | anchor: A05
A pedestrian crossing sign means slow down, be ready to stop, and yield to pedestrians crossing at intersections and crosswalks. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-F32 | anchor: A06
The slow-moving vehicle emblem must be shown on every vehicle traveling 30 mph or less on a public road, such as farm implements or animal-drawn vehicles, so adjust your speed or get ready to change lanes when you see it. [A06]
Why it matters: the emblem speed is a likely numeric item.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-F33 | anchor: A06
Slow down and pass animal-drawn vehicles slowly; from sunset to sunrise or in poor visibility they must carry a light or lamp visible within 500 feet. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-F34 | anchor: A06
A T-intersection ahead sign means your road ends soon, so get ready to turn right or left and yield to cross traffic. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-F35 | anchor: A06
If a curve sign shows a speed, slow to that speed for the curve. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-F36 | anchor: A08
A slippery road sign warns that the surface is slippery when wet and is often placed near bridges and overpasses. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec09-F37 | anchor: A08
A lane ends sign means two lanes are becoming one, and in the example shown the right-lane vehicles must yield and merge into the left lane. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec09-F38 | anchor: A08
A low clearance sign means you must not go on if your vehicle is taller than the height shown, or it may become stuck. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec09-F39 | anchor: A09
Orange signs with black letters mark construction and work zones, warning of restricted lanes, detours and other road work hazards, and you should slow down when you see one. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec09-F40 | anchor: A09
Drums, cones, tubes, flashing arrows and orange-and-white striped barriers keep traffic out of dangerous work areas, and you must always follow people directing traffic with orange signs, flags or stop signs. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec09-F41 | anchor: A09
Drivers who break the posted work zone speed limit while workers are present are fined $300. [A09]
Why it matters: the work zone fine appears in two chapters with different wording.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec09-F42 | anchor: A10
When a traffic signal is not working, treat the intersection as an uncontrolled intersection. [A10]
Why it matters: the dark signal rule is a likely test item.
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec09-F43 | anchor: A10
Do not enter an intersection with a traffic signal unless you can move through it immediately, continuously and completely without blocking cross traffic. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec09-F44 | anchor: A10
The gridlock rule does not apply when a traffic-control agent or peace officer directs you, when you are moving aside for an emergency vehicle with lights on, or when your turn lets you leave the intersection safely. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0068]

Misconceptions: a yield sign does not always require a full stop, only a stop when needed to give the right-of-way; an exempt sign at a crossing does not excuse anyone from looking for trains; a lane ends sign means the ending lane yields, not the through lane; a dark signal is not a green light.
Mnemonics: red rules and stops, yellow warns, orange works, green goes and guides, blue serves, brown shows the sights; a pentagon points to a school; the slow-moving vehicle emblem means thirty or slower.
Glossary: regulatory sign means a sign that states a law you must obey; crossbuck means the X-shaped railroad crossing sign; slow-moving vehicle emblem means the sign required on vehicles that travel at thirty mph or less on public roads; limited-use lane means a lane marked with a diamond for certain vehicles; gridlock means an intersection blocked by vehicles that entered without room to clear it.
Dynamic facts: the work zone speeding fine is an amount set by law that can change; recheck it against an official DPS source before each release.

corpus_stability.reason: The Minnesota Driver’s Manual prints a single edition line (June 2026) on its front cover and opens with a New laws and information chapter that collects recent changes in one place, with no sign of more than one rewrite per year in the selected pages.
